paragraphs.source_en: “Well, it is precisely because people make such a fuss over him that Dokusen manages to get by with that line of his. To begin with, that surname of his, Yagi, is wonderfully apt. Why, that beard of his is nothing but a goat’s beard. And he has had it growing in just that shape ever since his days in the school dormitory. His given name, Dokusen, is rather amusing too. In the old days, whenever he came to stay at my place, he would always hold forth to me about that negative sort of spiritual cultivation of his. He would repeat the same old tune over and over without ever stopping. I would say, ‘Come now, it’s time we went to sleep.’ But the fellow gave no thought to that and said unconcernedly, ‘I’m not sleepy.’ Then he would go right on discoursing about his negative theory, which put me in a terrible fix. At last, having no choice, I said, ‘You may not be sleepy, but I am desperately so, so please do go to bed.’ I finally got him to lie down, almost by pleading with him, but the matter did not end there. That night a mouse appeared and bit Dokusen on the tip of the nose. That set off a great commotion in the middle of the night. It seems that, for all his enlightened talk, the fellow still valued his life, and he became terribly anxious. He badgered me, saying, ‘If the mouse poison spreads through my whole body it will be dreadful; you must do something for me.’ I was at my wits’ end. In the end, having no other way out, I went to the kitchen, smeared a few grains of rice on a scrap of paper, and fooled him with that.”
